common.sin: Sine: a rule that turns an angle into a number. In a right triangle, it is opposite side divided by longest side.
common.cos: Cosine turns an angle into a number. For a sharp angle in a right triangle, divide the length of the adjacent leg by the length of the longest side. The adjacent leg touches that angle.
common.tan: Tangent: sine divided by cosine for the same angle.
common.tanh: Hyperbolic tangent: a calculator function whose answer stays between −1 and 1.
common.exp: The exponential rule: exp(x) means e raised to x, where e is about 2.718.
common.ln: Natural logarithm: the power you give e to make the input number. Here e is about 2.718.
common.log: Logarithm: the power needed to make the input number, using the base stated in the lesson.
common.Tr: Trace: add the entries along the main diagonal of a square matrix, from top left to bottom right.
common.diag: Make a matrix with these values on its main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
common.det: Determinant: one number made from a square matrix. For a two-by-two matrix, multiply the main-diagonal entries and subtract the other diagonal's product.
common.Var: Variance: the average squared distance of values from their average. It tells us their spread.
common.Cov: Covariance: how two quantities change together after their averages are removed.
common.Re: Real part: the part of a complex number that does not multiply the imaginary unit i.
common.Im: Imaginary part: the real number multiplying i in a complex number.
common.mean: Average: add the values and divide by how many there are, or use the stated probability weights.
common.Σ: Add the indicated terms. The small labels tell you which terms to include.
common.Δ: Change: the final value minus the starting value, unless this lesson states a different comparison.
common.ℏ: Reduced Planck constant: a fixed number connecting quantum energy to angular frequency. Read it as h-bar.
common.nm: Nanometres: one billionth of a metre each.
common.kg: Kilograms: a unit for mass, or how much matter an object has.
common.Hz: Hertz: cycles or readings per second, as named in this lesson.
common.Pa: Pascals: a unit of pressure, equal to one newton of force per square metre.
common.rad: Radians: an angle unit. One radian cuts off an arc as long as the circle's radius.
common.eV: Electronvolts: an energy unit equal to the energy change of one elementary charge across one volt.
common.MeV: Megaelectronvolts: one million electronvolts of energy.
common.GeV: Gigaelectronvolts: one billion electronvolts of energy. With c = 1, mass and momentum can use this unit too.
common.Mpc: Megaparsecs: a distance unit used for very large distances in space.
common.mol: Moles: groups containing the fixed Avogadro number of specified particles.
common.d: A tiny change. In dA/dt, divide the tiny change in A by the tiny change in time to find its rate. In an integral, d names the small pieces being added.
common.e: The exponential constant, about 2.718. Raising it to a changing power describes exponential growth, decay or phase.
common.Σⱼ: Add the terms for all allowed labels j.
common.Σₙ: Add the terms for all allowed numbers n.
common.log₂: Base-two logarithm: the power you give 2 to obtain the number in brackets.
common.ħ: Reduced Planck constant, read h-bar: the fixed number connecting quantum energy and angular frequency.
common.cot: Cotangent: cosine divided by sine for the same angle.
common.sinh: Hyperbolic sine: a calculator function used for growing and shrinking shapes.
common.cosh: Hyperbolic cosine: a calculator function used for growing and shrinking shapes.
common.sinc: Sinc: sine of the input divided by the input; its value at zero is 1.
common.lim: Limit: the value approached as the input gets closer to the stated number.
common.dim: Dimension: the number of independent directions in this state space.
common.cov: Covariance: a measure of how two quantities change together.
common.MJ: Megajoules: one million joules of energy.
common.au: Astronomical unit: about the average distance from Earth to the Sun.
common.arcsin: Inverse sine: find the angle whose sine equals the input number.

foundations.m: Metres: a unit of length or distance.

math.m: Metres: a unit of length or distance.
math.N₀: The starting amount N, when time is zero. The small zero labels the starting value.
math.ω₀: The natural angular frequency: how quickly the unforced oscillator repeats, measured in radians per second.
math.x: The input value, or horizontal position when a position is being studied.
math.v: Velocity: how fast position changes, including direction.
math.C: Coulombs, a unit of electric charge.
math.z: The z direction, perpendicular to the x and y directions.

mechanics.m: Metres: a unit of length or distance.
mechanics.N: Newtons: a unit of force, or push or pull.
mechanics.J: Joules: a unit of energy or work.
mechanics.v₀: The starting velocity, including its direction. The small zero means the value at time zero.
mechanics.ω₀: The starting angular velocity: the signed rotation rate at time zero.
mechanics.m₁: Mass of object 1: how much matter that object has.
mechanics.m₂: Mass of object 2: how much matter that object has.
mechanics.x₁: Position of object 1 along the chosen line.
mechanics.x₂: Position of object 2 along the chosen line.
mechanics.u₁: Velocity of object 1 before the collision.
mechanics.u₂: Velocity of object 2 before the collision.
mechanics.v₁: Velocity of object 1 after the collision.
mechanics.v₂: Velocity of object 2 after the collision.
mechanics.μm: μ × m: the gravity parameter GM multiplied by the orbiting object’s mass m.
mechanics.U: Potential energy: energy stored because of position or shape.
mechanics.ω: Angular velocity: how fast an object turns, including its turning direction.
mechanics.i: The label i means the starting value here.
mechanics.f: The label f means the final value here.

em.ε₀: Vacuum permittivity: the constant setting the electric-field scale in empty space.
em.μ₀: Vacuum permeability: the constant setting the magnetic-field scale in empty space.
em.ω₀: Natural angular frequency: how quickly this circuit oscillates when undriven, in radians per second.
em.q₁: Electric charge of object 1, including its sign.
em.q₂: Electric charge of object 2, including its sign.
em.E: Electric field: the force per unit of positive charge.
em.A: Area: how much surface is covered.
em.V: Voltage: energy change per unit of charge.
em.J: Current density: electric current per unit of area, with a direction.
em.I: Electric current: charge passing a point each second.
em.q: Electric charge on the object or plate being studied.

waves.ω₀: Natural angular frequency: the unforced, undamped oscillation rate in radians per second.
waves.A₀: Starting size of the oscillation amplitude.
waves.E₀: Starting energy in the decay formula, or peak electric-field size in a wave formula; the lesson identifies which quantity E represents.
waves.A₁: Amplitude, or peak size, of wave 1.
waves.A₂: Amplitude, or peak size, of wave 2.
waves.ε₀: Vacuum permittivity: the constant setting the electric-field scale in empty space.
waves.θ₁: Angle in medium 1, measured from the surface normal.
waves.θ₂: Angle in medium 2, measured from the surface normal.
waves.P_in: Power supplied: energy added each second.
waves.P_loss: Power lost: energy removed each second.
waves.p: Pressure; the prime mark here selects the small change from the resting pressure.
waves.I: Intensity: wave power reaching each unit of area.

thermodynamics.p_external: Pressure exerted on the system from outside.
thermodynamics.V: Volume: how much space the system occupies.
thermodynamics.T: Temperature, or the temperature whose change is written ΔT; use the scale specified in the lesson.

optics.θ_reflected: Angle of the reflected ray, measured from the line perpendicular to the surface.
optics.θ_incoming: Angle of the incoming ray, measured from the line perpendicular to the surface.
optics.θ_critical: The incidence angle at which the transmitted ray runs along the boundary.
optics.λ_material: Wavelength inside the material: the distance between repeating wave peaks.
optics.d_image: Image distance in the lesson’s sign convention. A following 1 or 2 identifies the relevant lens.
optics.d_object: Object distance in the lesson’s sign convention. A following 1 or 2 identifies the relevant lens.
optics.m₁: Signed magnification of the first lens: image size divided by object size.
optics.m₂: Signed magnification of the second lens.
optics.f_number: F-number: focal length divided by the entrance-pupil diameter.
optics.focal_length: Focal length: the lens’s distance scale for focusing parallel rays.
optics.pupil_diameter: Width across the entrance pupil, the apparent opening seen from the object side.
optics.f_objective: Focal length of the objective, the lens facing the distant object.
optics.f_eyepiece: Focal length of the eyepiece, the lens nearer the eye.
optics.I_out: Light intensity after passing through the stated device.
optics.I_in: Light intensity arriving at the device.
optics.I₁: Intensity from the first wave alone.
optics.I₂: Intensity from the second wave alone.
optics.n_j: Refractive index of section j: how much that section slows the light’s phase speed.
optics.I_max: Largest intensity in the interference pattern.
optics.I_min: Smallest intensity in the interference pattern.
optics.E_total: Total electric field after adding the wave contributions.
optics.I_image: Light intensity at the chosen image position.
optics.B₁: Brightness assigned to object point 1 in this image model.
optics.B₂: Brightness assigned to object point 2 in this image model.
optics.h₁: The image’s spread pattern from point 1, evaluated at the chosen image position.
optics.h₂: The image’s spread pattern from point 2, evaluated at the chosen image position.
optics.θ_R: Angular separation at the stated Rayleigh resolution limit.
optics.sampling_frequency: Number of samples per unit distance in this spatial-sampling lesson.
optics.pixel_pitch: Distance from one pixel centre to the next.
optics.ν_x: Spatial frequency in the x direction: cycles per unit distance.
optics.ν_c: Cutoff spatial frequency: the highest spatial frequency passed in the stated ideal model.
optics.n_cladding: Refractive index of the outer layer around a fibre’s core.
optics.n_core: Refractive index of the fibre’s inner core.
optics.n_effective: Effective index describing the phase speed of the chosen guided mode.
optics.I_photo: Electric current produced by the detected light.
optics.I: Light intensity: power reaching each unit of area.
optics.I₀: The reference light intensity, defined in the lesson.
optics.F: Fourier transform: a rule that rewrites a shape as a mix of waves.

atomic-nuclear.E_photon: Energy carried by the emitted or absorbed photon.
atomic-nuclear.E_separated: Energy of the same parts when they are separated, using the stated reference.
atomic-nuclear.E_bound: Energy of those parts in the bound state.
atomic-nuclear.binding_energy: Energy needed to separate the bound parts in the stated comparison.
atomic-nuclear.E_n: Energy of the state labeled by the integer n.
atomic-nuclear.L_z: Orbital angular momentum measured along the chosen z direction.
atomic-nuclear.E: Energy of the state being described.
atomic-nuclear.E_base: Energy from the simpler starting model.
atomic-nuclear.E_fine: Fine-structure energy contribution: a small correction from effects such as spin–orbit coupling. The preceding δ marks the correction.
atomic-nuclear.E_hyperfine: Hyperfine energy contribution: a still smaller correction involving nuclear properties. The preceding δ marks the correction.
atomic-nuclear.n_i: Occupation of complete electron state i: zero means empty and one means occupied.
atomic-nuclear.Z_effective: Effective nuclear charge: the approximate pull felt after other electrons partly screen the nucleus.
atomic-nuclear.sum_of_occupations: Add the electron counts in the listed complete states.
atomic-nuclear.gap_correction: Change made to the predicted energy gap by the improved model.
atomic-nuclear.improved_gap: Energy gap predicted by the improved model.
atomic-nuclear.reference_gap: Energy gap from the starting comparison model.
atomic-nuclear.net_stimulated_rate: Stimulated emission rate minus stimulated absorption rate.
atomic-nuclear.N_upper: Number of particles in the upper level.
atomic-nuclear.N_lower: Number of particles in the lower level.
atomic-nuclear.g_upper: Number of distinct states sharing the upper level’s energy.
atomic-nuclear.g_lower: Number of distinct states sharing the lower level’s energy.
atomic-nuclear.F: Force, or push or pull, along the separation direction.
atomic-nuclear.U_effective: Effective potential energy for the slow nuclear motion.
atomic-nuclear.E_electronic: Electron energy for the stated fixed nuclear separation.
atomic-nuclear.U_nuclear: Potential energy from the nuclei’s direct interaction.
atomic-nuclear.E_rotation: Energy stored in molecular rotation in this model.
atomic-nuclear.D_e: Energy from the bottom of the molecular well up to separated fragments.
atomic-nuclear.E_zero: Vibrational ground-state energy above the bottom of the well.
atomic-nuclear.r₀: Radius scale in the nuclear-size model, before multiplying by A to the one-third power.
atomic-nuclear.average_binding: Binding energy divided by the total number of protons and neutrons.
atomic-nuclear.B: Total nuclear binding energy in this equation.
atomic-nuclear.B_volume: The binding contribution associated with the bulk of the nucleus.
atomic-nuclear.B_surface: The binding reduction associated with nucleons at the surface.
atomic-nuclear.B_repulsion: The binding reduction from proton–proton electric repulsion.
atomic-nuclear.B_imbalance: The binding reduction associated with an imbalance between neutron and proton counts.
atomic-nuclear.δ_pair: The stated positive, negative or zero correction for pairing.
atomic-nuclear.E_next: Energy of the next available state above the filled group.
atomic-nuclear.E_filled: Energy of the highest filled state in this comparison.
atomic-nuclear.T_half: Half-life: time for the expected undecayed population to halve.
atomic-nuclear.daughter_change_rate: How quickly the daughter-nucleus count changes.
atomic-nuclear.production_rate: Number of daughter nuclei made per unit time.
atomic-nuclear.decay_rate: Number of daughter nuclei lost by decay per unit time.
atomic-nuclear.A_after: Total proton-plus-neutron count of the remaining nucleus after decay.
atomic-nuclear.Z_after: Proton count of the remaining nucleus after decay.
atomic-nuclear.E_gap: Energy difference between the two nuclear levels.
atomic-nuclear.E_recoil: Motion energy gained by the recoiling nucleus.
atomic-nuclear.total_charge_before: Add all electric charges before the process.
atomic-nuclear.total_charge_after: Add all electric charges after the process.
atomic-nuclear.energy_loss: Energy transferred from the traveling particle to its surroundings.
atomic-nuclear.stopping_power: Energy lost per unit distance in the stated material.
atomic-nuclear.N_signal: Estimated signal count after background and efficiency correction.
atomic-nuclear.N_observed: Count actually recorded by the detector.
atomic-nuclear.N_background: Estimated count from sources other than the desired signal.
atomic-nuclear.A_initial: Proton-plus-neutron count for each initial nucleus or nucleon in the sum.
atomic-nuclear.A_final: Proton-plus-neutron count for each final nucleus or nucleon in the sum.
atomic-nuclear.Z_initial: Proton number for each initial nuclear label in the stated reaction.
atomic-nuclear.Z_final: Proton number for each final nuclear label in the stated reaction.
atomic-nuclear.m_initial: Rest mass of each initial particle or nucleus in the sum.
atomic-nuclear.m_final: Rest mass of each final particle or nucleus in the sum.
atomic-nuclear.N_target: Number of target particles available for the reaction.
atomic-nuclear.E_CM: Total energy in the centre-of-momentum frame; “threshold” labels the minimum required value.
atomic-nuclear.final_rest_energies: The rest energies of all required outgoing particles, added together.
atomic-nuclear.released_energy: Energy made available by the decrease in total rest energy.
atomic-nuclear.initial_rest_energy: Total rest energy before the rearrangement.
atomic-nuclear.final_rest_energy: Total rest energy after the rearrangement.
atomic-nuclear.electric_potential_energy: Energy associated with the electric interaction of the two nuclei.
atomic-nuclear.stored_energy_change: Change in the energy kept inside the chosen system.
atomic-nuclear.generated_energy: Energy supplied inside the chosen system during the interval.
atomic-nuclear.escaping_energy: Energy leaving the system during the interval.
atomic-nuclear.N₀: Starting number of undecayed nuclei in the sample.
atomic-nuclear.D₀: Energy needed to dissociate the molecule from its vibrational ground state.
atomic-nuclear.I₀: Incident intensity before attenuation through the material.
atomic-nuclear.R₁: The measured decay count rate at the first time.
atomic-nuclear.R₂: The measured decay count rate at the second time.
atomic-nuclear.t₁: Time of the first rate measurement.
atomic-nuclear.t₂: Time of the second rate measurement.
atomic-nuclear.c: The speed of light in empty space.
atomic-nuclear.m: Mass; Δm means the difference between the starting and final total masses.
atomic-nuclear.δ: A small correction to the energy.
atomic-nuclear.T: The T with a one-half label means half-life: time for the expected undecayed count to halve.
atomic-nuclear.P: Radial probability density: multiplying by a tiny radial thickness gives the chance within that shell.
atomic-nuclear.ν̄: Antineutrino. The small e label selects the electron type.

particles.q_particle: Electric charge of the corresponding particle.
particles.q_up: Electric charge of an up quark.
particles.q_down: Electric charge of a down quark.
particles.proton_valence_label: The proton’s valence-quark label: uud means two up quarks and one down quark. It is not its complete quantum state.
particles.E_parent: Energy of the particle before it decays, in the chosen frame.
particles.E_products: Energies of the outgoing particles, all measured in the same frame.
particles.p_parent: Momentum of the particle before decay, including direction.
particles.p_products: Momenta of the outgoing particles; add their vector components.
particles.E_each: Energy of each outgoing particle in the stated equal-energy case.
particles.c: Speed of light in empty space.
particles.E_i: Energy of outgoing particle i in the chosen frame.
particles.p_i: Momentum of outgoing particle i in the same frame.
particles.E_CM: Total energy in the frame where total momentum is zero.
particles.B_i: Branching fraction for channel i: the share of decays taking that route.
particles.Γ_i: Decay width for channel i: its contribution to the overall decay rate, expressed in energy units.
particles.Γ_total: Total decay width after adding all channels.
particles.cross_section: Cross section: the effective area measuring how strongly the specified collision process occurs.
particles.L_integrated: Integrated luminosity: the accumulated beam-overlap exposure over the run.
particles.total_amplitude: The combined complex amplitude for the specified final outcome.
particles.contributing_amplitudes: The separate amplitude contributions leading to that same final outcome.
particles.leading_result: The first nonzero term kept in the approximation.
particles.B: Baryon number: a count-like label equal to one third of quark count minus antiquark count here.
particles.channel_yield: Expected event count for the selected final-state channel.
particles.production_rate: Rate at which the parent particle is produced.
particles.branching_fraction: Fraction of decays going into the selected channel.
particles.total_rest_frame_energy: All energy in the system’s rest frame, including motion and interaction energy of its parts.
particles.p_missing: Momentum imbalance inferred from the visible particles; the T label selects the part across the beam direction.
particles.p_visible: Measured visible-particle momenta; the T label selects their transverse parts.
particles.observed_count: Number of events actually recorded in the chosen sample.
particles.expected_background: Estimated count from known processes other than the proposed signal.
particles.σ_channel: Cross section already restricted to the selected channel; do not multiply its branching fraction a second time.
particles.total_charge_initial: Sum of all electric charges before the process.
particles.total_charge_final: Sum of all electric charges after the process.
particles.q: Electric charge, including its positive or negative sign.
particles.T: Teslas: a unit of magnetic field strength.
particles.m: Mass. In Δm², compare the squares of the two particle masses.

materials.vacancy_fraction: Fraction of lattice sites that are empty.
materials.total_sites: Total number of sites being counted.
materials.s_modulus: Young’s modulus: the material’s stiffness for small stretches along the stated direction.
materials.F_n: Net force on the atom or site labeled n.
materials.u_next: Displacement of the next site from its rest position.
materials.u_previous: Displacement of the preceding site from its rest position.
materials.u_n: Displacement of site n from its rest position.
materials.C_lattice: Heat capacity contributed by the lattice vibrations.
materials.occupancy_per_complete_electron_state: Number of electrons in one full state, including its spin label.
materials.occupied_count: Estimated number of occupied states in the chosen small energy interval.
materials.k_B: Boltzmann constant: the fixed factor connecting temperature to a particle-scale energy.
materials.E_gap: Energy gap between the specified states or bands.
materials.μ_mobility: Carrier mobility: drift speed per unit electric field. This μ is not a mass or a magnetic moment.
materials.n_intrinsic: Electron density of the pure intrinsic semiconductor; its hole density is the same.
materials.ρ_mobile: Net electric charge per volume carried by mobile electrons and holes.
materials.n_idealk_BT: n_ideal × k_B × T: diode ideality factor times Boltzmann constant times absolute temperature.
materials.P_out: Useful output power: energy delivered each second.
materials.P_in: Input power: energy arriving each second.
materials.ε₀: Vacuum permittivity: the constant setting the electric-field scale in empty space.
materials.E_final: Energy of the final electron state.
materials.E_initial: Energy of the initial electron state.
materials.E_exciton: Energy needed for the bound electron–hole excitation in this model.
materials.E_binding: Energy by which binding lowers the electron–hole pair relative to the unbound pair.
materials.M_net: Overall magnetization after combining the domains.
materials.volume_fraction: Fraction of the sample volume occupied by that domain.
materials.domain_magnetization: Magnetic moment per volume within that domain, including its direction.
materials.k_BT_c: k_B × T_c: Boltzmann constant times the critical temperature, an energy scale.
materials.E_conduction: Energy in the conduction band; “min” selects its lowest value.
materials.E_valence: Energy in the valence band; “max” selects its highest value.
materials.d_new: New spacing between the stated crystal planes.
materials.θ_new: New diffraction angle in the stated Bragg-angle convention.
materials.θ_old: Original diffraction angle in the same convention.
materials.n: The site number in the chain of atoms.
materials.m: Effective mass: the mass-like number describing how a particle responds inside the material.
materials.E: Energy; the plus or minus sign selects the upper or lower energy.
materials.μ: Mobility when labeled mob, n or p: how quickly a carrier drifts for a given electric field.
materials.χ: Susceptibility: how strongly the material responds to the applied field. The e or m label selects electric or magnetic response.

quantum1.i: Imaginary unit: the number defined by i² = −1. It lets amplitudes carry a phase.
quantum1.ψ: The quantum state or wavefunction, read “psi.” Its amplitudes are used to predict measurement chances.
quantum1.x: Position along the chosen x direction.
quantum1.H: Hamiltonian: the operator describing energy and governing how the state changes with time.
quantum1.E₁: Energy of state 1 in the stated model.
quantum1.E₂: Energy of state 2 in the stated model.
quantum1.u_i: Basis pattern labeled i. Here i is a label, not the imaginary unit.
quantum1.σ_x: Standard deviation of position: the spread of position outcomes.
quantum1.σ_p: Standard deviation of momentum: the spread of momentum outcomes.
quantum1.p₀: Starting mean momentum of the wave packet.
quantum1.P: Probability: the chance of the stated result, from 0 to 1.
quantum1.j: The label of the measured outcome.
quantum1.a: The left end of the position interval.
quantum1.b: The right end of the position interval.
quantum1.V: Potential energy, which can change with position.
quantum1.L: Orbital angular momentum: the quantum quantity describing motion around a point.
quantum1.L̂: The rule for finding orbital angular momentum; the hat marks it as an operator.
quantum1.Y: The angular wavefunction: how the state depends on direction.
quantum1.m_ec: m_e × c: electron mass times the speed of light. In m_ec², only the speed is squared.

quantum2.i: Imaginary unit: the number defined by i² = −1. It lets amplitudes carry a phase.
quantum2.ψ: The quantum state or wavefunction, read “psi.” Its amplitudes are used to predict measurement chances.
quantum2.x: Position along the chosen x direction.
quantum2.H: Hamiltonian: the operator describing energy and governing how the state changes with time.
quantum2.I: Identity operator: it leaves a state unchanged.
quantum2.U†: The conjugate transpose of U; for a unitary gate, this undoes U.
quantum2.A: The observable operator being studied: a rule associated with measurement outcomes.
quantum2.B: The second observable operator in the stated comparison.
quantum2.u_j: Component j of state u in the chosen basis.
quantum2.v_j: Component j of state v in the same basis.
quantum2.Σ_j: Add the terms for every allowed label j.
quantum2.Σ_i: Add the terms for every allowed label i.
quantum2.Σ_k: Add the terms for every allowed label k.
quantum2.Σ_a: Add the terms for all distinct allowed values labeled a.
quantum2.z: The chosen z direction used as a reference for the measurement.
quantum2.S_z: The spin angular-momentum operator along z.
quantum2.ρ: Density matrix: a table of amplitudes and weights used to predict measurements of a pure state or a mixture.
quantum2.ρ_AB: Density matrix of systems A and B together.
quantum2.ρ†: The conjugate transpose of ρ: swap rows and columns and reverse the imaginary parts.
quantum2.P: The probability or projector named P in this lesson; a projector selects a specified outcome subspace.
quantum2.α₀: Starting complex amplitude of the coherent state.
quantum2.χ: The spin-state part of the full state in the stated space-times-spin separation.
quantum2.a₀: Amplitude for outcome 0 in the first qubit’s state.
quantum2.a₁: Amplitude for outcome 1 in the first qubit’s state.
quantum2.b₀: Amplitude for outcome 0 in the second qubit’s state.
quantum2.b₁: Amplitude for outcome 1 in the second qubit’s state.
quantum2.σₓ: Pauli x matrix: the operation that swaps the two basis amplitudes.
quantum2.P₀: Probability starting from state 0; the arrow to 1 specifies transfer into state 1.
quantum2.E: Energy. The plus or minus label selects one of the two energies.
quantum2.J: Angular momentum: the quantum quantity describing rotation.
quantum2.J₁: Angular momentum of the first part of the system.
quantum2.J₂: Angular momentum of the second part of the system.
quantum2.J_+: Raising operator: moves the angular-momentum state up by one allowed component step.
quantum2.J_-: Lowering operator: moves the angular-momentum state down by one allowed component step.
quantum2.S: Spin angular momentum: the particle’s built-in quantum rotation quantity.
quantum2.j: The label of the total angular-momentum size, or an outcome label in a measurement sum.
quantum2.m: The row or state label m in the displayed expression.
quantum2.n: The column or state label n in the displayed expression.
quantum2.Ψ: The two-particle quantum state. The plus or minus label selects its exchange symmetry.
quantum2.λ: An eigenvalue: an allowed value associated with the matrix.
quantum2.σ_A: Standard deviation of A: the typical spread of its measurement results.
quantum2.σ_B: Standard deviation of B: the typical spread of its measurement results.
quantum2.σ_y: Standard deviation of the y component: its measurement spread.
quantum2.σ_z: Standard deviation of the z component: its measurement spread.
quantum2.φ: The part of the wavefunction describing positions.

quantum3.i: Imaginary unit: the number defined by i² = −1. It lets amplitudes carry a phase.
quantum3.ψ: The quantum state or wavefunction, read “psi.” Its amplitudes are used to predict measurement chances.
quantum3.x: Position along the chosen x direction.
quantum3.H: Hamiltonian: the operator describing energy and governing how the state changes with time.
quantum3.m: Mass of the moving particle in the stated model.
quantum3.c: Speed of light in empty space.
quantum3.V: Potential-energy or interaction operator specified in this lesson.
quantum3.Σ_i: Add the terms for every allowed label i.
quantum3.Σ_j: Add the terms for every allowed label j.
quantum3.Σ_l: Add the angular-momentum channels labeled l.
quantum3.γ₁: Population-relaxation rate: how quickly excited-state population falls.
quantum3.S_rate: Survival probability predicted by the stated constant-rate approximation.
quantum3.P_transfer: Probability transferred to the specified destination state or set of states.
quantum3.ρ_E: Density of final states per unit energy.
quantum3.χ: Nuclear-motion amplitude in the stated separation of electron and nuclear motion.
quantum3.C₀: Coulomb-potential strength in the stated hydrogen-like model.
quantum3.Eₘ: Energy of the state labeled m; the superscript (0) means the unperturbed value.
quantum3.U₀†: Inverse of the unperturbed evolution operator U₀.
quantum3.E: Energy; a plus or minus label selects one of the displayed levels.
quantum3.Eₙ: Energy of state n. A raised number in brackets labels the correction order, not a power.
quantum3.c_f: Amplitude for reaching the final state f. A raised (1) marks the first-order estimate.
quantum3.j: Probability current: how quickly probability moves past a point.
quantum3.s: The running position used while adding the small pieces in the integral.

quantum3.u: A normalized state of the displayed matrix.

advanced-mechanics.S: Action: the Lagrangian added up over the chosen time interval.
advanced-mechanics.m: Mass: how much matter the modeled object has.

advanced-mechanics.p: Canonical momentum paired with q. For the simple cart, it is mass times velocity.
advanced-mechanics.V: Potential energy: energy associated with position in the chosen force model.
advanced-mechanics.H: Hamiltonian: the function of coordinates and momenta that gives their motion rules; it equals total energy in the stated simple models.
advanced-mechanics.E: The conserved total energy in the stated model.
advanced-mechanics.ℓ: Length of the pendulum from its pivot to its mass.
advanced-mechanics.v: Velocity: how quickly position changes, including direction.
advanced-mechanics.r: Distance from the centre, or the position vector from the chosen origin when written as a vector.
advanced-mechanics.V_eff: Effective radial potential: the ordinary potential plus the angular-momentum barrier.
advanced-mechanics.ω_same: Angular frequency of the mode in which the two masses move together.
advanced-mechanics.ω_opposite: Angular frequency of the mode in which the two masses move in opposite directions.
advanced-mechanics.y: Vertical position in the chosen coordinate system.
advanced-mechanics.m_i: Mass of the piece labeled i in the sum.
advanced-mechanics.ω: Angular velocity: how fast the body turns and about which direction; for a single oscillation it names angular frequency.
advanced-mechanics.L_rot: Rotational angular momentum of the rigid body.
advanced-mechanics.ω_i: Angular-velocity component along principal axis i.
advanced-mechanics.i: The label selecting one of the three principal axes.

advanced-mechanics.F: Force along the chosen coordinate: a push or pull, including its sign.
advanced-mechanics.E_top: Pendulum energy at its upright top position, using the bottom as zero potential energy.
advanced-mechanics.θ: Pendulum angle measured from its downward rest direction.
advanced-mechanics.Ω: Angular frequency of the external driving force.
advanced-mechanics.t_n: Time of sample n in the repeated-sampling sequence.
advanced-mechanics.nT_d: n × T_d: sample number n multiplied by one driving period.
advanced-mechanics.Q: New canonical coordinate after the stated change of variables.
advanced-mechanics.P: New canonical momentum paired with Q.
advanced-mechanics.α: Positive strength of the attractive potential V = −α/r in the orbit model.
advanced-mechanics.φ: Orbital angle. When it appears as a subscript on p, it names the coordinate whose canonical momentum is being used.
advanced-mechanics.q₁: Displacement of mass 1 from its rest position.

advanced-mechanics.r₀: Radius of the circular orbit being tested.
advanced-mechanics.I₁: Principal moment of inertia about axis 1.
advanced-mechanics.I₂: Principal moment of inertia about axis 2.
advanced-mechanics.I₃: Principal moment of inertia about axis 3.
advanced-mechanics.δ₀: Starting separation between the two nearby trajectories.
advanced-mechanics.k: Spring stiffness: how much more force is needed for each extra stretch.
advanced-mechanics.x: Position in the fixed reference frame.
advanced-mechanics.p_φ: Angular momentum for the angle φ. It stays fixed when the forces exert no torque about that axis.
advanced-mechanics.f: The function being studied; in a constraint equation, f = 0 sets the allowed positions.
advanced-mechanics.K: Stiffness of the spring joining the two objects.
advanced-mechanics.h: The height of the moving support at the given time.
advanced-mechanics.ḣ: How quickly the support height changes: its vertical velocity.
advanced-mechanics.ẋ: Velocity in the fixed frame: the rate of change of x.
advanced-mechanics.λ: The constraint multiplier: a number that lets us include the constraint force.
advanced-mechanics.I_z: Moment of inertia about the z axis: resistance to changing the turning motion about that axis.
advanced-mechanics.x_i: The x position of mass piece i.
advanced-mechanics.y_i: The y position of mass piece i.
advanced-mechanics.I_i: Moment of inertia about principal axis i.
advanced-mechanics.τ₁: Torque about principal axis 1: the turning effect of the applied forces.
advanced-mechanics.β: The strength of the extra cubic spring-force term.
advanced-mechanics.γ: Damping rate: how strongly the motion is slowed in this model.
advanced-mechanics.A: The size of the driving term in the angular-acceleration equation.
advanced-mechanics.δ: Distance between two nearby states being compared.
advanced-mechanics.F₂: A generating function: a rule used to change position and momentum coordinates together.
advanced-mechanics.W: The position-dependent part of the action.

fluid-dynamics.A: Cross-sectional area of the flow passage.
fluid-dynamics.v: Flow velocity or its stated component; subscripts 1 and 2 select the two sections.
fluid-dynamics.h: Distance between the two parallel surfaces.
fluid-dynamics.y: Position along the y direction, often measured away from the wall.
fluid-dynamics.z: Position along the z direction, upward in the hydrostatic example.
fluid-dynamics.u: Flow velocity component in the x direction.
fluid-dynamics.p: Fluid pressure: normal push per unit area.
fluid-dynamics.ρ: Mass density: fluid mass per volume.
fluid-dynamics.μ: Dynamic viscosity: the coefficient relating shear stress to a velocity gradient.

fluid-dynamics.L_model: Reference length in the scale model.

fluid-dynamics.fₓ: x component of force per unit volume.

fluid-dynamics.τ: Shear stress: sideways force per unit of area.
fluid-dynamics.D: The capital D marks change while following a moving bit of fluid.

fluid-dynamics.r: Distance from the centre of the pipe.
fluid-dynamics.L: The chosen length scale; for a pipe segment, its length.
fluid-dynamics.gₓ: The x part of gravitational acceleration.
fluid-dynamics.u_out: Signed fluid velocity leaving the region.
fluid-dynamics.u_in: Signed fluid velocity entering the region.
fluid-dynamics.Ma: Mach number: fluid speed divided by the local speed of sound.
fluid-dynamics.F_D: Drag force: the force opposing motion through the fluid.

plasma.λ_D: Debye length: the distance scale over which mobile charges screen a small electric disturbance.
plasma.ε₀: Vacuum permittivity: the constant setting the electric-field scale.
plasma.k_B: Boltzmann constant: the factor converting temperature into a particle-scale energy.
plasma.n_e: Electron number density: electrons per volume.
plasma.n: Particle number density: number of particles per volume in the stated population.
plasma.m: Mass of the charged particle being followed.
plasma.ω_p: Plasma angular frequency: the natural collective charge-oscillation rate in the stated model.
plasma.φ: Electric potential: electric potential energy per unit charge.
plasma.B: Magnetic-field strength, or magnetic-field vector when a direction is needed.
plasma.E: Electric field: force per unit charge, including direction.
plasma.v_perp: Particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
plasma.n_s: Number density of species s; the label identifies the kind of particle.
plasma.u_s: Average flow velocity of species s.
plasma.ω: Angular frequency of the wave, in radians per unit time.
plasma.k: Wave number: how quickly the wave phase changes with distance.
plasma.c_s: Ion-sound speed in the stated electron-and-ion approximation.
plasma.v_A: Alfvén speed: the speed of the stated magnetic-tension wave in the fluid model.
plasma.μ₀: Vacuum permeability: the constant setting the magnetic-field scale.
plasma.v: Individual particle velocity in the distribution integral.
plasma.f: Velocity distribution: particle density per velocity interval in this one-dimensional model.

plasma.u_x: Average particle velocity in the x direction.
plasma.λ₁: Initial Debye screening length in this comparison.
plasma.A₀: Disturbance amplitude at the starting time.
plasma.ω_c: Cyclotron angular frequency: how fast a charged particle circles in the magnetic field.
plasma.q: Electric charge of the particle, with its sign.
plasma.n_i: Number of ions per unit of volume.
plasma.B_m: Magnetic field strength at the mirror point, where the motion along the field reverses.
plasma.B₀: Magnetic field strength at the starting point.
plasma.α₀: Starting angle between the particle velocity and the magnetic field.
plasma.D_s: Change while following the flow of particle type s.
plasma.D: Together with Dt, marks a rate while following the moving particles.
plasma.q_s: Charge of one particle of type s.

general-relativity.c: Speed of light in empty space.
general-relativity.τ: Proper time: time measured by a clock following the stated path.
general-relativity.t: Time coordinate in the chosen description.
general-relativity.a_near: Free-fall acceleration at the nearer point.
general-relativity.a_far: Free-fall acceleration at the farther point.

general-relativity.A: The vector whose components are being rewritten.
general-relativity.g_μν: Metric component with lower labels μ and ν; the metric tells how coordinate changes combine into an interval.
general-relativity.V: The vector being moved or differentiated.
general-relativity.Γ: Connection coefficient: the correction accounting for how the coordinate directions change from place to place.

general-relativity.ν: A component label running over the four spacetime coordinates. Here a raised letter is an index, not a power.
general-relativity.α: A component label running over the four spacetime coordinates. Here a raised letter is an index, not a power.
general-relativity.β: A component label running over the four spacetime coordinates. Here a raised letter is an index, not a power.
general-relativity.σ: A component label running over the four spacetime coordinates. Here a raised letter is an index, not a power.
general-relativity.ρ: A component label running over the four spacetime coordinates. Here a raised letter is an index, not a power.
general-relativity.R_μν: Ricci tensor component: a particular sum of spacetime-curvature components.
general-relativity.a_relative: Acceleration of one nearby falling object relative to the other.
general-relativity.p: Pressure of the fluid measured in its local rest frame.
general-relativity.G_μν: Einstein tensor component: the combination of Ricci curvature and its trace used in the gravity equation.
general-relativity.T: Stress-energy tensor: the collection describing energy, momentum and stresses. Its labels select one component.
general-relativity.g_00: Time–time metric component in the stated coordinates. Both small zeros select the time direction.
general-relativity.r_s: Schwarzschild radius: the horizon radius in the nonrotating, uncharged black-hole model.
general-relativity.G_N: Newton’s gravitational constant: the fixed strength factor in Newton’s gravity law.
general-relativity.M: Mass of the spherical gravitating source.
general-relativity.f_far: Light frequency measured by the stationary receiver far away.
general-relativity.f_emit: Light frequency measured at the supported emitter.
general-relativity.r_emit: Radius of the emitter in the Schwarzschild coordinates.
general-relativity.D: Physical separation of the two comoving points at the same cosmic time.
general-relativity.χ: Fixed comoving coordinate separation; it uses distance units in this lesson.
general-relativity.Λ: Cosmological constant, a term allowed in Einstein’s gravity equation.
general-relativity.s: The spacetime interval label. Its square combines small changes of time and position.
general-relativity.l: Distance along a small spatial step.
general-relativity.g: Metric: the numbers that turn coordinate steps into physical intervals.
general-relativity.g_xx: Metric number multiplying the two x steps.
general-relativity.g_xy: Metric number for the mixed x and y steps.
general-relativity.g_yy: Metric number multiplying the two y steps.
general-relativity.r: Distance from the centre in these polar coordinates.
general-relativity.θ: Angle around the centre in these polar coordinates.
general-relativity.R: Curvature. With several indices it is the Riemann tensor; alone it is scalar curvature, a single combined number.
general-relativity.ξ: Small separation between the nearby freely falling objects.
general-relativity.L: The original length of the arm.
general-relativity.a: Scale factor: the number telling how cosmic distances grow or shrink.

experimental-methods.n: Number of readings in the sample.
experimental-methods.t: Time; Δt is the gap between consecutive readings.

experimental-methods.f_sample: Sample rate: number of readings taken each second.
experimental-methods.f_max: Highest signal frequency the measurement is intended to capture.

quantum-information.P: Probability of the outcome written in brackets: a number from zero to one.
quantum-information.a: Complex amplitude attached to |0⟩ in the first qubit.

quantum-information.p: The probability specified in this lesson, from zero to one.
quantum-information.ρ: Density matrix: the state’s table of weights and phase information used to predict measurements.
quantum-information.ρ_out: Density matrix after the stated operation.
quantum-information.ψ_in: Input quantum state, before the gates.
quantum-information.ψ_out: Output quantum state, after the gates.

quantum-information.P_fail: Probability that the encoded information has a logical error after the stated recovery.
quantum-information.O_f: Phase oracle for function f: multiplies each basis state by (−1) raised to its function value.

quantum-information.f: The specified function whose output is either 0 or 1.
quantum-information.a_i: Amplitude of item i in the search state.
quantum-information.v: The normalized state representing the measurement outcome being tested.
quantum-information.K_j: One of the channel operators: rules describing the possible effects of the noise. The j labels which rule.

many-body.n: Occupation: number of particles in the specified complete single-particle state.

many-body.a_j: Remove a boson from site or mode j.

many-body.Σ_i: Add the contribution from every site or mode i.
many-body.U: Interaction-energy cost per on-site pair in the specified model.
many-body.E_bond: Energy contributed by the single bond between two neighboring spins.
many-body.s_i: Ising spin at site i, either +1 or −1.

many-body.A: The first quantity or observable being averaged and compared.

many-body.m: Average Ising spin in these mean-field lessons, between −1 and +1.

many-body.s: One Ising spin variable, with outcomes +1 and −1.

many-body.Σ_ij: Add over all ordered pairs of site labels i and j in this definition.
many-body.M: Total dimensionless spin in the stated response model.
many-body.χ: Susceptibility: how much the mean total spin changes per small change of its applied field energy.
many-body.z: Number of nearest neighbors of one site.
many-body.J: Interaction strength: the energy scale connecting two neighboring spins.

many-body.σ: Standard deviation of one input quantity: the typical spread of its values.

many-body.δ: A small change from the original value.

quantum2/displacement-operator.D†: Inverse of the unitary displacement operator D, undoing that displacement.

quantum2/density-from-preparations.c_n: Component n of the pure state’s amplitude column; the star means complex conjugate.

quantum3/instantaneous-eigenstates.a: The time-dependent state coefficients; the following m or n selects which energy-state coefficient.

quantum3/kraus-channel-bridge.K: A channel operator; the small 0 or 1 identifies which of the two displayed terms.

quantum3/packets-and-elastic-regime.j_j: Incident particle flux for component j: particles arriving per area and time.

quantum2/two-level-capstone.U: Time-evolution operator: the rule taking the initial state to its later state.

advanced-mechanics/circular-orbit-radius.dV_eff: A tiny change in the effective radial potential energy.

waves/small-pendulum.ℓ: Distance from the pivot to the swinging mass.
waves/small-pendulum.T₀: Time for one small swing cycle, out and back.

waves/two-mass-equations.ẍ₁: Acceleration of the first cart, with rightward taken as positive.
waves/two-mass-equations.ẍ₂: Acceleration of the second cart, using the same direction.

optics/single-aperture.θ₁: Angle from straight ahead to the first dark band.

optics/finite-double-slit.d: Distance between the centres of the two slits.
optics/finite-double-slit.θ: Angle from straight ahead to the point on the viewing screen.
optics/finite-double-slit.α: Phase angle set by the separation of the two slits.
optics/finite-double-slit.β: Phase angle set by the width of one slit.

optics/snell-index.n₁: Refractive index of the material the light starts in.
optics/snell-index.n₂: Refractive index of the material the light enters.
optics/snell-index.θ₁: Angle of the incoming ray from the line perpendicular to the surface.
optics/snell-index.θ₂: Angle of the transmitted ray from that same perpendicular line.

astrophysics/distance-errors.L: Luminosity: total light power that the source gives off.
astrophysics/distance-errors.F: Flux: light power received per unit area.

foundations/vectors.x: The east–west part of the displacement.
foundations/vectors.y: The north–south part of the displacement.
